name: sandbox-terminal
changelog: v7: an SSH client that disconnects while its command is still starting (a stopped sandbox booting, a terminal opening) no longer leaves that command running in the sandbox — the tile waits for the manager to say which command it started, then ends it (HUP, then killed) as for one that leaves while it runs; GET /sessions stops listing a connection once its client has gone. v6: security fixes — its SSH server runs on golang.org/x/crypto v0.57.0 (was v0.48.0), fixing ten advisories its code reaches (GO-2026-5013, -5014, -5017, -5018, -5019, -5020, -5023, -6303, -6354, -6355: certificate and FIDO-key restrictions bypassed, source-address options not enforced, panics, deadlocks and loops a client can cause); its go.mod now says go 1.26.0, which that release needs. v5: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager signs its fake coding agent in with the agent's own login command and can take a smaller stdin limit — nothing changes for people or managers. v4: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager offers the contract's optional stdio capability (a split exec's stderr apart, a non-tty exec's streams on one WebSocket) — nothing changes for people or managers. v3: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager advertises an image's coding agents (hello.images[].harnesses) and gives a terminal TERM, COLORTERM and LANG — nothing changes for people or managers. v2: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager follows the contract's optional ports capability (D135) — nothing changes for people or managers. v1: terminals onto coding sandboxes for people, over the sandbox-manager contract — its page lists the sandboxes shared with it by manager and opens browser terminals straight to the manager as tabs (reattaching to running ones, ending them), and SSH (ssh <sandbox>@host -p 2222) with keys registered per person on the page — every login asks xbind whether the key's person still has access to the tile (removed or disabled: access revoked, their keys kept inactive); a native view lists them and manages keys (terminals open in the browser); sandboxes reach it by being shared with it
title: Sandbox terminals
description: Terminals onto coding sandboxes for people, in the browser and over SSH. Bind it to one or more sandbox managers (the coding-sandbox template, or any tile implementing /docs/sandbox-manager.md); a sandbox shows up here once its owner shares it with this tile. People register their SSH public keys on its page and log in with ssh <sandbox>@host -p 2222 after an admin publishes the port (bx expose apps/sandbox-terminal ssh=runtime --listen :2222). No port forwarding, agent forwarding or sftp.
